Q: How to trigger a callback only when the router is called? A:

Actually by accident, I did exactly what I wanted. The dcc.Location has 4 different triggers:

  • href ("http://127.0.0.1:8050/page-2?a=test#quiz")
  • pathname ("/page-2")
  • search ("?a=test")
  • hash ("#quiz")

Meaning that by listening only to pathname, my callback will not be triggerred when I alter the search or the hash of the said url.

If one want to get a trigger on every little change then listen to href:

@callback(
    Output("landing_tracker", "children"),
    Input("url", "href"),
    State("magic_session", "data"),
    prevent_initial_call=False,
)
def track_visit(url, session_data):
    """Track landing page visit with session ID."""
    pattern, url = route_to_pattern(__name__), urlparse(url).path
    if session_data and session_data.get("session_id")  and pattern.match(url):
        telemetry.add_page_visit(session_data["session_id"], "landing_page")
    return ""

Q: HTTP Toolkit setting invalid NODE_OPTIONS A:

This is a new issue in recent versions of Next.js, which seem to have changed how NODE_OPTIONS (that are otherwise valid if you just run node directly) are interpreted. Bug fix coming soon, in the meantime you may be able to resolve this by downgrading your Next.js version temporarily. There's some ongoing discussion in https://github.com/httptoolkit/httptoolkit-server/issues/168 and the attached PR.

Q: Add Tailwind CSS classes manually without pre-declaration in HTML code A:

Case of fully meaningful class names

e.g.: hidden, bg-sky-500, overflow-auto, etc.

If you implement the class using JavaScript, then the class becomes part of the JS code. You need to configure Tailwind CSS to also scan the JS code for valid Tailwind CSS class names. In this way, it will detect the class name embedded in the JS and include it in the generated CSS.

TailwindCSS v4

By default, it comes with automatic source detection, which does this for you. It only ignores paths in node_modules and .gitignore. You can modify this afterward: use @source to add extra paths or @source not to disable them.

  • What's breaking changes from v4?
  • Automatic Source Detection from TailwindCSS v4 (instead of content property)
  • Adding an external source or a package from within node_modules for detection
TailwindCSS v3

You need to manually declare the paths in the content property of tailwind.config.js. In a React.js project, it is recommended to include the jsx and tsx files as well, as suggested in the documentation:

  • https://v3.tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/nextjs (There is no separate React.js guide, but the principle is the same.)
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
module.exports = {
  content: [
    "./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}",
  ],
  theme: {
    extend: {},
  },
  plugins: [],
}

Class names that cannot be clearly inferred

e.g.: bg-{$js_var}, h-[calc(${$js_var}_+_10px)], etc.

Your question, therefore, does not concern fully defined class names—without an example, we cannot know exactly—but rather dynamic class names, where it is not immediately inferable even with human logic what you mean. For this reason, Tailwind CSS cannot interpret them as classes either.

  • How do you reference dynamic classes/utilities using a JS variable and pass them through in the class attribute inline in HTML?

In these cases, the safelist not only doesn't help - it can actually do more harm. For example, declaring bg-*, text-*, border-*, etc. classes for every color is completely useless and wasteful: generation will be slow, the generated CSS will be large, and in most cases 50-80% of it will never be used. Instead, you should always rely on CSS variables and transfer the values of JS variables into CSS variables. I covered this in more detail in the previously linked answer.
